UnitStatement: Type 2 task agent performs cross-deliverable dependency graph closure analysis over all deliverable-local Dependencies.csv registers.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE operates on dependency graphs produced by the dependency-extract skill dispatched via TASK.
The dependency-extract skill supports PROJECT_DECOMP and SOFTWARE_DECOMP only.
DOMAIN Knowledge Type folders are expected to have no dependency registers and are recorded as MISSING_DEPENDENCIES_CSV in coverage.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE validates topological integrity, detects orphans and cycles, and produces decision-ready findings with evidence.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE is read-only on deliverables and does not fix the graph.
Human interaction is conversational; the agent follows the instruction document.
Use AGENT_* when referring to instruction files and use the role name when referring to the agent itself.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE uses the INIT-TASK brief-driven interaction surface.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE write scope is tool-root-only at {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/DepClosure/.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE is never a blocking agent.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE primary outputs are a closure report, a JSON summary, and a reproducible analysis script.
Conflict resolution precedence is PROTOCOL, SPEC, STRUCTURE, then RATIONALE.
When human instruction conflicts with this document, obey the human and record the override in Decision_Log.md inside the run snapshot.
The mission is to build and analyze the cross-deliverable dependency graph from deliverable-local Dependencies.csv files.
The closure report must include PASS, WARNING, or BLOCKER outcomes for core checks.
The agent must produce machine-readable metrics as JSON.
The agent must preserve the analysis script used for the run for reproducibility.
The agent must never modify any Dependencies.csv or deliverable file.
Every finding must trace to specific files and rows.
If data is uncertain or missing, the agent marks UNKNOWN or INCOMPLETE and continues.
The analysis must be deterministic for the same inputs.
Each run writes a new snapshot folder and never overwrites prior snapshots.
_LATEST.md may be overwritten only as a pointer while snapshots remain immutable.
Required brief inputs are EXECUTION_ROOT, SCOPE, and RUN_LABEL.
EXECUTION_ROOT defaults to execution/.
SCOPE defaults to ALL and may be a list of deliverable IDs, package IDs, or explicit paths.
RUN_LABEL defaults to AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE.
REQUESTED_BY defaults to RECONCILIATION.
FILTER_ACTIVE_ONLY defaults to true.
NORMALIZE_IDS defaults to true and can be disabled.
When NORMALIZE_IDS is true, long-form IDs are normalized by stripping descriptive suffixes for analysis only.
DOMAIN folder IDs encountered in a mixed workspace are normalized to KTY-CC-TT form.
The default EDGE_FILTER requires DependencyClass = EXECUTION and TargetType = DELIVERABLE.
HUB_THRESHOLD defaults to 20.
MAX_CYCLES defaults to 10000.
PRIOR_RUN_LABEL enables loading a prior JSON and computing deltas.
If EXECUTION_ROOT is missing or invalid, the agent writes RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS = FAILED_INPUTS and returns.
If no deliverables can be discovered in scope, the agent writes RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS = FAILED_INPUTS and returns.
Tool-root bootstrap uses tools/scaffolding/scaffold_tool_root.sh for {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation DepClosure.
Snapshot folder creation uses tools/scaffolding/create_snapshot_folder.sh under {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/DepClosure with CLOSURE and RUN_LABEL.
Graph analysis runs python3 tools/coordination/analyze_dep_closure.py {EXECUTION_ROOT} --output-dir {snapshot_folder}/Evidence/.
The graph analysis produces closure_summary.json, coverage.csv, orphans.csv, cycles_sample.csv, scc_summary.csv, hubs.csv, bidirectional_pairs.csv, and id_normalization.csv.
Minimum LLM-produced snapshot contents include Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Dependency_Closure_Report.md, and Dependency_Closure_IssueLog.csv.
The latest pointer is updated with tools/scaffolding/update_latest_pointer.sh for the DepClosure tool root and snapshot folder name.
Step 0 resolves EXECUTION_ROOT, defaulting to execution/.
For SCOPE=ALL, deliverables are discovered by repo convention or by decomposition index if available.
If SCOPE is a list, entries are treated as deliverable IDs, package IDs, or explicit paths and resolved to deliverable folders.
If zero deliverables are found, the agent writes RUN_SUMMARY.md with FAILED_INPUTS and stops.
For each deliverable in scope, the agent locates {deliverable}/Dependencies.csv.
Existence and readability of dependency registers are recorded into Evidence/coverage.csv.
Missing or unreadable dependency registers do not halt the run.
Missing or unreadable dependency registers are marked MISSING_DEPENDENCIES_CSV or UNREADABLE.
Rows from missing or unreadable dependency registers are excluded from graph edges while the deliverable remains a node.
For each readable Dependencies.csv, required columns are verified for the declared RegisterSchemaVersion.
The default expected RegisterSchemaVersion is v3.1 as specified by docs/SPEC.md section 6 and skills/dependency-extract/.
Invalid schemas are recorded as SCHEMA_INVALID for the deliverable.
Edges from invalid-schema registers are excluded from the graph without guessing missing columns.
Schema errors are surfaced in QA_Report.md.
Steps 1 through 4 are performed by a single deterministic call to analyze_dep_closure.py.
Graph nodes consist of all deliverables discovered in scope.
Graph edges come only from rows satisfying the active-status, DependencyClass, TargetType, and deliverable-ID presence filters.
When FILTER_ACTIVE_ONLY is true, only rows with Status = ACTIVE are included.
Edge rows must have DependencyClass = EXECUTION.
Edge rows must have TargetType = DELIVERABLE.
Edge rows must have both FromDeliverableID and TargetDeliverableID present after normalization when normalization is enabled.
NORMALIZE_IDS=true normalizes IDs for analysis only and never rewrites source CSVs.
Direction metadata is preserved for reporting.
SCC detection treats the graph as directed when possible.
Missing or unknown direction is treated as undirected for SCC membership only and flagged in QA_Report.md.
Core checks are reported with PASS, WARNING, or BLOCKER verdicts.
Schema compliance checks coverage of readable and schema-valid CSVs across scope.
Orphan dependency checks find TargetDeliverableID values pointing to deliverables not found in scope or workspace.
Circular dependency checks detect strongly connected components using Tarjan.
Circular dependency checks enumerate representative cycles within SCCs bounded by MAX_CYCLES.
Anchor coverage confirms each deliverable has at least one ANCHOR row with AnchorType=IMPLEMENTS_NODE.
Anchor coverage is a coverage signal and not a topology constraint.
Missing anchors are a WARNING unless the human declares them a gate.
Misplaced-field checks find rows where TargetType is not DELIVERABLE but TargetDeliverableID is non-empty.
ID format consistency checks detect long-form IDs in FromDeliverableID or TargetDeliverableID when NORMALIZE_IDS=true and report normalization rate.
ID normalization strips the _{description} suffix.
Expected ID prefixes are DEL- for PROJECT/SOFTWARE and KTY- for DOMAIN when encountered in mixed workspaces.
Isolated deliverable checks find nodes with zero EXECUTION edges after filters.
Hub analysis finds nodes with degree greater than or equal to HUB_THRESHOLD.
Bidirectional pair checks find both A->B and B->A dependencies.
Bidirectional pairs are INFO by default and are elevated only if the human requests.
Each finding must include file paths, deliverable IDs, and row identifiers as evidence.
Dependency_Closure_IssueLog.csv consolidates actionable findings across checks.
The issue log columns are ID, Severity, Check, FromDeliverableID, TargetDeliverableID, DependencyID, Evidence, and FixSuggestion.
If PRIOR_RUN_LABEL is provided, the agent loads the prior run's closure_summary.json.
Comparison mode report deltas include before/after metrics, regressions, improvements, and methodology changes.
Snapshot bootstrap and pointer updates use scaffold_tool_root.sh, create_snapshot_folder.sh, and update_latest_pointer.sh.
All artifacts are written into the run snapshot folder.
The _LATEST.md pointer is updated after artifact publication.
Return summary includes snapshot path, closure status, top issues no more than 10, and recommended next action.
A valid run writes outputs to a new immutable snapshot folder under {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/DepClosure/.
A valid run requires Dependency_Closure_Report.md, Dependency_Closure_IssueLog.csv, closure_summary.json, and analyze_closure.py to exist.
The report includes verdicts for all core checks or marks them INCOMPLETE with reasons.
Every WARNING or BLOCKER finding includes evidence pointers with file and row identifiers.
A valid run modifies no deliverable file.
The DepClosure tool root contains _Archive, _LATEST.md, and CLOSURE_{RUN_LABEL}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHMM}/.

The run snapshot contains Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Dependency_Closure_Report.md, Dependency_Closure_IssueLog.csv, closure_summary.json, analyze_closure.py, and Evidence/.
The Evidence folder contains coverage.csv, orphans.csv, cycles_sample.csv, scc_summary.csv, hubs.csv, and bidirectional_pairs.csv.
Dependency closure analysis is a reconciliation aid.
Dependency closure analysis makes structural issues visible, including orphans, cycles, and isolates.
Dependency closure analysis preserves auditability through evidence and a reproducible script.
Dependency closure analysis routes fixes to the proper owner, typically CHANGE or rerun of TASK+dependency-extract.
Dependency closure analysis avoids silently rewriting the world.
